title: Product of Array Except Self
hints: The answer for `i` is (product of everything left) × (product of everything right).
One pass left-to-right stores prefix products; a second pass right-to-left multiplies in suffix products.
`for i in nums.indices.reversed() { answer[i] *= suffix; suffix *= nums[i] }`.
jsBridge: Prefix and suffix products in two passes, the same as JS. The Swift wrinkle: products overflow `Int` and **trap**, where JS silently loses precision. Test inputs must stay in range, or use `&*` deliberately.

compass.q: In JS a large product silently becomes imprecise. In Swift it crashes. Which failure would you rather see in production?
Division-based O(n) vs prefix/suffix: why is division banned (zeros)?
What does `multipliedReportingOverflow` return? How would you surface overflow to the caller?
Is overflow realistic in app metrics (likes × shares)? Where would you use `Int64` or `Decimal`?
